text:
Maya: Quick sync — need final decisions on the prod-entry thresholds for the Dedicated pilot. Main buckets: SLA banding, minimal docs, oncall/support handoff, monitoring dashboards, and pricing for burst vs committed. Can we lock owners and deadlines today?
Alex: Can you clarify what you mean by SLA banding? do you want discrete tiers or per-customer SLOs?
Maya: Discrete tiers to start (bronze/silver/gold). We can do per-customer later. Tiers should map to latency SLOs, uptime, and support response windows.
Jordan: For latency let's call out p95/p99 for inference and p50 for health checks. Suggested initial defaults:

```
bronze: p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 900ms, uptime 99.5%, support response 8h
silver: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 700ms, uptime 99.9%, support response 4h
gold:   p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 350ms, uptime 99.95%, support response 1h
```

Jordan: Also need error-rate SLO: <1% for bronze, <0.5% for silver, <0.2% for gold.
Priya: Support: reply windows are fine but also need to specify what counts as incident vs ticket. Who triages first? Is it our Platform oncall or a sales-tiered concierge for gold?
Sam: From Sales: gold customers expect white-glove onboarding + a direct Slack channel. Also we want discounting for 12/24mo commitments. Need to know what SLA we can commit to before we promise discounts.
Ravi (Finance): Pricing impact: gold SLAs increase cost by ~18-25% due to reserved slot warming and higher oncall costs. If we offer 10% discount for 12mo gold, margin goes thin. We should model three pricing options tied to the tiers.
Elena: Docs scope: minimal public pieces + internal runbooks. Public: SLA summary page, pricing matrix, FAQ, and a short "what to expect at onboarding". Internal: runbook with escalation paths, playbook for throttling/fallbacks, monitoring dashboard guide. I can draft public docs if owners and content bullets are clear.
Maya: Good. Let's capture owners now. Jordan = monitoring + SLO definitions + dashboard templates. Elena = public SLA page + pricing matrix. Priya = support/playbook + triage definition. Alex = product owner for tier mapping and rollout policy. Ravi = pricing modeling final. Sam = customer promises and discount thresholds.
Alex: For rollout policy: start with silver enforcement for all pilot customers, allow opt-in to gold for a fee and capacity commit. Keep bronze as best-effort for small customers. Is that acceptable?
Jordan: Fine, but we need autoscaling safety nets. If a gold customer bursts beyond reserved capacity we need an automated fallback to a compatible model variant with a clear API response indicating degraded SLA. We'll add a fallback codepath and a flag in the response.
Priya: Oncall: Platform oncall handles detection/auto-remediation. Tiered human escalation: bronze -> Platform L2 -> product oncall; silver -> Platform L2 -> Product L1 -> Customer Success; gold -> Platform L1 + named CS + 24/7 escalation. Need names for the rotations.
Maya: Naming convention: L1 = 1hr response, L2 = 4h. Priya please propose rotation plan by EOD.
Elena: For the public SLA doc I need the exact SLO numbers (Jordan) and the supported fallback behaviors (Jordan + Alex) and a summary of remedies (credits) — Legal will want language for credits.
Ravi (Finance): On credits: propose capped credits = min(monthly bill, 10%) for silver, 25% for gold in severe breaches. Need legal to approve. Also we should precompute expected quarterly cost delta for each tier.
DeployBot: [deploy] Dashboard template "sla-band-template-v1" was created by Jordan in #dashboards (link: https://dashboards/redwood/sla-band-template-v1)
Sam: For go-to-market, we need a one-pager (sales play) explaining tradeoffs, and an FAQ on whether customers can mix tiers across models. Also want recommended pricing bands (list price, committed discount, overage).
Jordan: Monitoring items: dashboard + alerting playbook + synthetic runners for critical endpoints (cold vs warm latency). I'll attach the synthetic job names in the doc.
Maya: Action summary (owners + due dates):
- Jordan: finalize SLO table, error-rate definitions, fallback behavior doc. Due: 48h.
- Elena: public SLA page + pricing matrix draft. Due: 72h.
- Priya: oncall rotation proposal + triage matrix. Due: EOD today.
- Alex: rollout policy + opt-in flow for gold. Due: 72h.
- Ravi: pricing delta + credits proposal. Due: 72h.
- Sam: sales play one-pager + FAQ bullets. Due: 72h.
- Maya: consolidate and publish acceptance checklist once drafts in. Due: 96h.
Maya: Any blockers I missed?
Priya: Need legal language for credits and SLA exceptions. Can we get Legal review?
Maya: I'll ping Legal. @channel anyone who wants to be on the review loop add yourself here.
Alex: I'll add a feature flag gating the enforcement for 2 weeks post-rollout so we can observe.
Sam: heads-up: two pilot customers already asked for gold — will not promise until we have doc + price.
Maya: OK — thanks all. I'll compile owners into the checklist and post an updated thread after Priya's rotation plan lands. :thumbsup:
